hypothese.summary: AWS accelerates for a 5th consecutive quarter (36.7% in Q2, backlog +36% sequentially to $496bn) and its margin holds up better than feared (39.4%, +650bp) despite the heaviest capex cycle in the group's history, now raised to ~$220bn for 2026 (vs ~$200bn guided at Q1) on memory-cost inflation. Published net income ($62.6bn, EPS $5.75) is in reality driven more than 90% by a $53.4bn non-operating mark-to-market gain on the Anthropic stake - fully excluded from the Omnium model, which judges the company on its operating AWS/NA/International. Free cash flow keeps deteriorating (TTM -$7.6bn vs +$18.2bn a year ago) and the balance sheet flipped to positive net debt in H1 2026, with $67bn of new long-term debt issued in six months - confirming and amplifying the debt-funded scenario already anticipated. omniumEPS 7.95->14.27 (2026-2030, +16.4% vs the 2025 EPS restated to 6.83$ once the Anthropic gains already embedded in published FY2025 are likewise excluded, and the non-recurring Leo/Kuiper costs are added back to 2026-2028 earnings).
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
The AWS/AI leadership bet strengthens - at full price. Cloud reaccelerated to +36.7% (backlog 496bn; AI and in-house silicon each above 25bn run-rate) and AWS margin EXPANDED to 39.4% (vs 37.7%), contradicting the compression risk flagged last refresh. The cost side: FY26 capex raised to ~220bn (+67% vs 2025) and the balance sheet flipped to net debt (+5.9bn end-June vs -57.4bn end-2025) after 67bn of new long-term debt in six months. Published net is flattered by the Anthropic revaluation gain, excluded from the Omnium base.

== THESIS READ ==
- AWS margin resilience under peak capex is the quarter's key evidence - the thesis's central risk did not materialize this period. Watch: whether 39%+ holds as depreciation from the 2025-26 capex wave lands.
- The balance-sheet flip is structural: net debt peaks ~30bn in 2026, returns to net cash by 2028 on the model's FCF path. Watch: further issuance pace vs FCF inflection.
- No buybacks (confirmed again: zero in financing flows) - dilution +1.1%/yr continues; financial income/charges are recalculated yearly at 10Y+2pts on the AVERAGE net position per E5-a bis - the bridge's finNet sign flips through the plan as the position crosses zero. Watch: any first-ever buyback signal.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = normalized GAAP: ex-Anthropic gain and identified one-offs. Normative tax 21% (FY25 actual ~15% NOT reconducted, per E5-b - documented as the published-year residual driver). Consensus basis wedge documented in the scorecard (adjusted non-GAAP street vs normalized GAAP Omnium).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Revenue +15% 2026 fading to +9.5% by 2030; EBIT margin 13.2% -> 15.7% (AWS mix); ETR 21%; shares +1.1%/yr. Watch: AWS margin vs depreciation wave; retail international profitability; Kuiper capitalization; consensus-basis wedge at each snapshot.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); AWS re:Invent (Dec) AI bookings; 2027 capex framing; FCF inflection evidence.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 26: net sales $197-202B (sequential decel explained by the Prime Day shift INTO Q2 - ex-Prime-Day growth would be ~400bp higher - and ~80bp FX headwind); operating income $22.5-26.5B.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 cash capex RAISED to ~$220B (from ~$200B) on memory cost inflation - and still NOT enough capacity for 2026 or 2027 demand; AWS power capacity to double by end-2027 vs 2025 (on track); no annual P&L guidance (constant practice).
pointsCles: Q2 26: revenue $200.6B (+20% ex-FX, beat ~$4B, includes Prime Day shifted into Q2), operating income $27.5B (+43%) incl ~$1.2B of one-offs (tariff refunds ~$600M NA + ~$600M energy-derivative fair-value gain in AWS); GAAP EPS $5.75 vs consensus 1.82 - the gap is the bridged Anthropic MTM + one-offs, recurring base ~$1.82.

AWS is inflecting: +36.7% to $42.2B (5th straight acceleration, fastest in 18 quarters, +$4.6B sequential ~80% above the prior record), $169B run rate, backlog $496B growing triple-digit with most 2027 capacity already reserved and striking 2028 bookings; AWS margin 39.3% (+650bp, +520bp ex-derivative) on efficiency and custom silicon.

Chips are a >$25B run-rate business growing triple-digit: Trainium carries multiyear multi-gigawatt commitments from BOTH Anthropic and OpenAI plus startup adoption, and selling Trainium OUTSIDE the cloud is under active discussion ('real chance'); Graviton on 98% of top-1000 EC2 customers; own frontier model coming ('half a dozen comparable models, one of them ours') while Bedrock stays multi-model.

Capex raised to ~$220B for 2026 (memory inflation) with demand still exceeding capacity through 2027; Jassy frames the economics (data centers 30+yr life monetized across 5-6 server generations, servers break even <3yrs on >=5yr AI contracts) and LIFTS the ambition: AWS 'at least double a few hundred billion', possibly a $1 trillion revenue business; stores side: 2nd-largest US grocer, same-day perishables in 2,300 cities changing the essentials trajectory, ads +26% to $19.8B.

ancrages.moteur: FY2026 capex raised to ~220 Md$ (vs ~200 Md$ in Q1 26, +67% vs 131,8 Md$ in 2025), monetisation still guided as 'mainly 2027-2028' -> extends and amplifies the D&A pressure on the 2027-2028 exit margin beyond the previous assumption, despite the margin resilience observed in Q2 26.

AWS growth stepped up to 36,7% YoY in Q2 26 (vs 28% in Q1), backlog +36% sequentially to 496 Md$ (vs 364 Md$ in Q1) with triple-digit YoY growth -> modestly raises the consolidated revenue growth trajectory for 2026-2027 vs the previous assumption, with gradual deceleration thereafter towards ~9,5% in 2030.

Mark-to-market gains on the Anthropic stake (53,4 Md$ pre-tax in Q2 26 alone, ~69,4 Md$ cumulative over H1 2026) remain non-operating, highly volatile and symmetrically reversible -> full exclusion from the adjXXX maintained across the whole horizon.

North America margin stable at 7,9% (Q1 and Q2 26, plateau after the 2024-25 expansion) and International margin continuing its convergence (3,6% Q1 -> 4,1% Q2) -> gradual expansion trajectory carried forward for both segments, with the NA pace slightly tempered vs the previous assumption (plateau observed rather than a linear continuation).

67 Md$ of new long-term debt issued in H1 2026 (LT debt almost doubled, 65,6 -> 128,9 Md$), net cash position swung from -57,4 Md$ (FY25) to +5,9 Md$ as early as end-June 2026 (earlier and larger than previously projected) -> omniumND revised up and the return to a net cash position pushed back to 2028 (vs 2027 in the previous thesis) given FY26 capex raised to 220 Md$ and partly debt-financed.

No explicit funding rate communicated by management this quarter -> default rule applied: US 10-year Treasury (4,67% at 30/07/2026) + 2pts of normative spread = 6,67%, applied symmetrically to the projected average ND (positive or negative) each year; no regular buyback programme identified, hence no zero-rate exception on the net cash.

Normative tax rate maintained at 21%; the implied FY2025 effective rate (markedly lower, combined with a favourable net financial effect while the company was in a net cash position) is not carried forward as it is not representative of a normalised base (rule E5-b, an abnormal rate is never carried forward as is).

Continued net dilution through RSU share-based compensation, no net buyback programme identified this quarter either (H1 26 financing flows: debt only, zero share buybacks) -> extrapolated at +~1,1%/yr across the whole horizon, unchanged vs the previous thesis.

Reported FY2025 operating income (79 975 M$) included ~4,6 Md$ of non-recurring charges (FTC Prime settlement ~2,5 Md$, severance ~2,7 Md$, Italian tax dispute + legal settlement ~1,1 Md$, store impairments ~0,6 Md$) already identified in the previous thesis but never adjusted in `data` (E5 d-bis compliance failure, corrected at this refresh) -> `data` 2025 now adjusted: ebit 84 600 M$ (margin 11,80%), net 82 150 M$ (the same reported net/EBIT conversion rate of 97,1% retained so as not to introduce an artificial break).

Reported Q2 26 OI (27,5 Md$) includes ~1,2 Md$ of non-recurring benefits (customs tariff refund ~0,6 Md$ + accounting gain on AWS derivatives ~0,6 Md$) -> neutralised in the H1 2026 base used to build the bottom-up FY2026 estimate (normalised H1 ~50,1 Md$ of EBIT rather than the 51,3 Md$ reported).

Reported FY2025 net income (77 670 M$) already included ~10,0 Md$ of pre-tax gains tied to Anthropic in 'Other income (expense), net' (7,7 Md$ of revaluation of the non-voting preferred stock + ~2,3 Md$ of reclassification on the conversion of convertible notes in Q3 2025, confirmed by the 10-K FY2025 'Other Income' note), not adjusted in the previous thesis even though these gains are of the same nature as those excluded from the projections -> `data` 2025 now adjusted (net 73 350 M$, ~19,63% effective rate for FY2025 as reported in the 10-K applied symmetrically to the removal/add-back) for a comparison base consistent with the full exclusion of Anthropic over the projected horizon.

At the user's explicit request: the non-recurring ramp-up costs of Amazon Leo/Kuiper (~1 Md$/quarter flagged by the CFO for Q2 26, satellite launch/deployment cost ahead of commercial monetisation) are treated as a negative exceptional and added back to earnings rather than left as a permanent drag -> addback +4,0 Md$ in 2026, +2,5 Md$ in 2027, +1,0 Md$ in 2028, nil thereafter as the commercial service (targeted Q3 2026) begins to monetise. Point to be re-verified at the next refresh as soon as Amazon isolates an explicit recurring Leo cost/revenue.
